stories.title: WIRED: an Accenture contractor connected a Defense Department coding environment holding controlled unclassified information to a personal Claude Code account; the agent appears to have sent login credentials and a map of the NIPRNet system to a high-risk third-party site; Accenture says the allegations were investigated and found 'without merit'

Cohere makes the first close of a Series E targeting up to C$7B at a C$35.7B valuation, the largest private round in Canadian start-up history; Schwarz Group leads, the Government of Canada commits up to $1.14B (Bloomberg) and Cohere plans ~$1.2B of computing in Canada by 2030; ARR up 165% in a year

Baseten's Base Labs releases joey-1, a 2B open-weight (MIT) decision model post-trained from Qwen3.5-2B that returns a calibrated probability instead of text: P50 20 ms per 2,000-token request at $0.01 per M tokens; best model under 4B on the Jev Decision Index 0.4 public split (63.30, #37 of 230)

Anthropic study: 50 causal-inference analysts working with Claude Code followed their agent's secretly coin-flipped preference on 86% of analytical choices; 77% reused the agent's arguments to explain their choices but only 15% credited the agent

FuriosaAI raises a $620M Series D at a $2.9B post-money valuation (from $735M last year) for its RNGD inference accelerator, in mass production since January: 20,000 cards this year and memory and fab capacity secured for more than 40,000 in 2027; Korea's National Growth Fund puts in about $280M

Amazon keeps 2026 cash capex at about $220B, mostly for AWS, and says it will spend 'meaningfully more' in 2027; AWS revenue up 39% to a $184B run-rate and Jassy forecasts about 40% growth in 2027 and 2028, repeating that AWS can become a $1T-a-year business

Thrive Holdings, the OpenAI-backed holding company that buys businesses to rebuild them with AI, acquires home-security firm ADT for $10 a share (~$7.6B equity, $15.3B enterprise value); OpenAI supplies models and forward-deployed engineers to its 75+ companies

The Information: DeepSeek and Moonshot leaned heavily on OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra outputs to train their latest models, including Kimi K3.1 Pro and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, after Anthropic's defences cut extractable data by 90-99%; Moonshot declined to comment (via The Decoder)

Open-source tinyworldformer runs a 26k-131k-parameter int8 looped-transformer world model on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W microcontroller, generating Breakout, Pong, Flappy Bird, Doom-lite and Pac-Man frames while a 9k-16k-parameter agent plays and learns inside the generated game (Hacker News front page)

Ex-Palantir executives launch Dream with a $17M a16z-led seed to build 'built world models' trained on 100M+ square feet of US permit data, generating structurally sound building designs to replace hand-drawn work in AutoCAD and Revit
Deepgram acquires Daily, maker of the open-source Pipecat voice-agent framework, for an undisclosed sum and commits to keeping Pipecat open source and vendor-neutral

NYT: US intelligence surveilled Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore AI-cloud firm Megaspeed (earlier investigated over reselling restricted Nvidia chips to China), for about a year over concern she was gathering information on Nvidia and Jensen Huang's lobbying; Nvidia says regional customers get no sensitive information

Bloomberg: Anthropic is SpaceX's 'Customer B', 34.5% of SpaceX's Q3 revenue via compute from its AI unit, now bigger than the US government; Anthropic can spend up to $120.5B through 2029 (~$3.1B a month from December) but can cancel on 90 days' notice after early 2027

Sam Altman says OpenAI will point its robotics programme at building data centres and calls 'self-replicating data centers' within grasp; says OpenAI's own chip does well on intelligence per watt and that sandboxes work only 'to a point' against far smarter AI (Cheeky Pint podcast)

Bloomberg reports Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum (~$85B), whose lasers for AI data-centre optical links are sold out to early 2029, likely in stock; a deal could come as soon as next week but is not agreed (via TNW)
OpenAI doubles Work and Codex usage limits on its Pro 100 and Pro 500 plans and reverses a planned cut on Pro 200; Plus is unchanged and Dots usage is tracked separately (via The Decoder)

Mistral releases the weights of Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk'): ~1T-parameter multimodal MoE (49B active, 1M context) under a modified-MIT 'Ecosystem' licence that excludes model-as-a-service; Terminal-Bench 4.0 41% (from 28% in preview), 48% on Artificial Analysis's Coding Agent Index with 47% fewer tokens than GLM-5.3, 51% Cyber Index
